question: What is the primary function of the stratum corneum in the epidermal layer?

options.A: Providing a tough lipid-embedded barrier against moisture loss and pathogens
options.B: Supplying rich vascular perfusion to nourish the upper epithelial cells
options.C: Synthesizing melanin pigment to protect against ultraviolet radiation
options.D: Producing sebum to maintain the natural acid mantle of the body

explanation: The stratum corneum is composed of keratinized cells and lipids that form the main protective shield against dehydration and microbial invasion. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h1)

question: How does the acid mantle protect the integumentary system from disease?

options.A: By lowering surface pH to inhibit the growth of pathogenic bacteria
options.B: By stimulating rapid cell division within the dermal blood vessels
options.C: By neutralizing alkaline chemical exposures from harsh soaps
options.D: By increasing lipid production to prevent excessive solar radiation

explanation: The slight acidity of the skin surface creates an unfavorable environment for colonization by harmful microorganisms. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h1)

question: When is the most effective time to apply an emollient or moisturizer to the skin?

options.A: Right before exposing the body to direct sunlight outdoors
options.B: Immediately after bathing while the skin is still damp
options.C: Strictly at bedtime after completing all daily physical exercises
options.D: Only when severe scaling and cracking become clearly visible

explanation: Applying moisturizers to damp skin helps trap and seal water molecules directly into the superficial layers of the epidermis. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h2)

question: Why are harsh alkaline soaps discouraged for routine daily hygiene?

options.A: They stimulate excessive sebum production leading to bacterial overgrowth
options.B: They block sweat glands and prevent normal thermoregulation processes
options.C: They instantly cause permanent chemical burns on the stratum corneum
options.D: They strip away protective surface lipids and disrupt the acid mantle

explanation: Alkaline soaps raise skin pH and remove vital protective oils, leaving the skin vulnerable to dryness, irritation, and infection. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h2)

question: Which vitamin acts as a vital cofactor for collagen synthesis and tissue repair?
explanation: Vitamin C is essential for the hydroxylation steps required to cross-link collagen fibers during skin healing and maintenance. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h3)

question: A patient with chronic protein malnutrition is at high risk for skin breakdown primarily because:

options.A: The epidermis thickens and blocks all normal absorption of moisture
options.B: Collagen synthesis and cellular proliferation are severely impaired
options.C: Subcutaneous fat stores increase and compress superficial capillaries
options.D: The sweat glands stop producing the natural protective acid mantle

explanation: Proteins supply the fundamental building blocks needed for skin matrix formation, cellular regeneration, and tensile strength. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h3)

question: What is the primary skin pathology associated with cumulative ultraviolet radiation exposure over time?
explanation: Ultraviolet radiation causes cumulative DNA mutations and breakdown of dermal elastic fibers, leading to skin malignancies and premature aging. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h4)

question: A hospital ward nurse who performs frequent hand washing develops dry, red, scaling hands with minor fissures. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Frequent washing and chemical exposure strip the epidermal barrier, frequently resulting in non-allergic irritant contact dermatitis among healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h4)

question: What is the primary physiological cause of tissue necrosis in pressure injuries?

options.A: Excessive systemic dehydration causing superficial epidermal peeling
options.B: Prolonged capillary occlusion leading to localized tissue ischemia
options.C: Direct bacterial invasion through intact sweat gland openings
options.D: Accumulation of excess subcutaneous fat compressing nerve endings

explanation: External pressure exceeding capillary closing pressure cuts off oxygen and nutrient supply, causing ischemia and tissue death. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h5)

question: Which nursing action directly minimizes the risk of shear injury when moving a patient in bed?

options.A: Elevating the head of the bed to a high Fowler position constantly
options.B: Using a draw sheet or lifting device to avoid dragging the body
options.C: Massaging reddened bony prominences vigorously with alcohol lotion
options.D: Applying heavy waterproof dressings over all major joint areas

explanation: Lifting devices and draw sheets prevent friction and parallel sliding forces that tear underlying dermal blood vessels during repositioning. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h5)

question: In the ABCDE criteria for evaluating pigmented skin lesions, what does the letter 'B' represent?
explanation: In the melanoma screening mnemonic, B stands for border irregularity, denoting ragged or poorly defined lesion margins. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h6)

question: Why is the 'E' (Evolving) component of the ABCDE criteria considered particularly critical during a self-examination?

options.A: It proves that the lesion has expanded beyond six millimeters in diameter
options.B: It indicates that the superficial lipid barrier of the epidermis has failed
options.C: Any noticeable change in an existing mole often signals malignant transformation
options.D: It confirms that the skin lesion has become infected with normal flora

explanation: Changes over time in size, shape, color, or symptoms are hallmark indicators that a mole requires professional dermatological evaluation. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h6)

question: Which physiological change in older adults contributes significantly to an increased risk of skin tears?

options.A: Thinning and atrophy of the dermal layer
options.B: Rapid thickening of the stratum corneum
options.D: Excessive production of natural skin oils

explanation: Aging causes dermal thinning, flattening of the epidermal junction, and loss of elasticity, making the skin fragile and prone to tears. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h7)

question: A patient with long-standing diabetes mellitus asks the nurse how to care for their feet at home. Which instruction is most appropriate?

options.A: Apply strong chemical corn removers directly to any hard skin areas on your toes
options.B: Inspect your feet daily for cuts, redness, or blisters using a mirror if needed
options.C: Soak your feet in hot water every evening to soften calluses and improve circulation
options.D: Walk barefoot around the house to keep the foot muscles strong and flexible

explanation: Because diabetic neuropathy masks pain, daily visual inspection is essential to catch minor injuries before they develop into severe ulcers. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T9#GNS213_U5_T9_h7)
